table.name: badges
table.purpose: Badges awarded to users (StackExchange-style data dump). One row per badge awarded to a user; a user can earn the same badge multiple times (e.g. tag-based badges).

col_001.name: badge_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the badge award row.

col_002.name: user_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to users.id; the user who received the badge. Many badges per user (many-to-one).

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Badge name. Mostly standard StackExchange badge names (Student, Supporter, Editor, Scholar, Teacher, Autobiographer, Analytical...), but also tag-based badges whose name is a tag (correlation, nonparametric, modeling, pca, Outspoken). 153 distinct names.

col_004.name: date
col_004.description: Timestamp when the badge was awarded, ranging from 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14.

table.name: comments
table.purpose: Comments on posts (StackExchange-style data dump: each row is one comment made by a user on a post).

col_001.name: comment_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the comment.

col_002.name: post_id
col_002.description: ID of the post (question or answer) the comment was made on; references posts.col_001 (many comments per post).

col_003.name: score
col_003.description: Score of the comment (net upvotes). Mostly 0, small non-negative integers, occasional high outliers (max 90).

col_005.name: creation_date
col_005.description: Timestamp when the comment was created (2009-02-02 to 2014-09-14).

col_006.name: user_id
col_006.description: ID of the user who wrote the comment; references users.col_001. Null for ~1.6% of comments (likely deleted/anonymized users).

col_007.name: user_display_name
col_007.description: Display name of the commenting user, populated only when user_id is null (e.g. 'user10525' for deleted accounts, or a real name).

table.name: postHistory
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style post history / revision log: one row per edit or lifecycle event on a post (initial body, title/tag edits, closures, deletions, etc.), referencing the post and the acting user.

col_001.name: Id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the post-history event.

col_002.name: PostHistoryTypeId
col_002.description: Code for the type of history event (e.g. initial question/answer body, title edit, body edit, tag edit, close/reopen, delete/undelete, etc.). 25 distinct codes, 1-38, matching the Stack Exchange PostHistoryTypeId enumeration; exact per-code meanings not verifiable from the data alone. Alternative reading: an internal event-category code not following the Stack Exchange enumeration, though the value range and count fit it well.

col_003.name: PostId
col_003.description: Foreign key to posts.Id; the post this history event applies to.

col_004.name: RevisionGuid
col_004.description: UUID grouping the revisions of a single edit (all events of one revision share the same GUID); all-zero GUID appears for non-revision events.

col_005.name: CreationDate
col_005.description: Timestamp when the history event occurred.

col_006.name: UserId
col_006.description: Foreign key to users.Id; the user who caused the event. Null (or -1) for events by deleted/anonymous users or system actions.

col_007.name: Text
col_007.description: The content captured by the event: post body/title/tags at that revision (values like '<regression>', '<r>', question/answer text). Empty for events without content.

col_008.name: Comment
col_008.description: Editor's comment describing the change ('edited title', 'added 1 characters in body', 'removed signature and greetings'); empty for most events.

col_009.name: UserDisplayName
col_009.description: Display name of the acting user when no user account applies (e.g. 'user10525'); empty when UserId is set.

table.name: postLinks
table.purpose: Links between posts (Stack Overflow-style PostLinks table): each row records a relationship between two posts, such as duplicate or related links, with the date the link was created.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of the post link row; unique integer identifier.

col_002.name: creation_date
col_002.description: Timestamp when the link was created.

col_003.name: post_id
col_003.description: Id of the source post in the link (references posts.id).

col_004.name: related_post_id
col_004.description: Id of the target/related post in the link (references posts.id).

col_005.name: link_type_id
col_005.description: Link type code: 1 = duplicate (dominant, ~92%), 3 = related. Only these two values occur; consistent with the Stack Exchange PostLinks enum. Alternative reading: a generic link category code whose labels are not documented in the database itself.

table.name: posts
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style Q&A posts (questions and answers, apparently from the Cross Validated / statistics site), one row per post. Questions and answers are mixed in this table, distinguished by post type; answers point to their question via a parent id.

col_001.name: PostId
col_001.description: Primary key of the post. Referenced by postHistory, comments, postLinks, tags and votes.

col_002.name: PostTypeId
col_002.description: Post type code: 1 = question (~43k rows), 2 = answer (~48k rows); rare values 4-7 likely wiki/tag-wiki/moderator-nomination etc. Exact mapping of 3-7 is not verifiable from the data alone.

col_003.name: AcceptedAnswerId
col_003.description: Id of the answer accepted as the solution; set only on questions that have an accepted answer (hence ~84% null). Values fall in the post-id range.

col_004.name: CreationDate
col_004.description: Date and time the post was created.

col_005.name: Score
col_005.description: Net vote score (upvotes minus downvotes); can be negative (min -19).

col_006.name: ViewCount
col_006.description: Number of views; populated only for questions (null for answers, ~53% null).

col_007.name: Body
col_007.description: Post body in HTML (questions and answers).

col_008.name: OwnerUserId
col_008.description: Id of the user who created the post; references users.col_001. -1 denotes a system/anonymous owner.

col_009.name: LastActivityDate
col_009.description: Timestamp of the last activity (edit, answer, comment) on the post.

col_010.name: Title
col_010.description: Post title; only questions have titles (null for answers, ~53% null).

col_011.name: Tags
col_011.description: Question tags in angle-bracket format, e.g. <regression><r>; only on questions.

col_012.name: AnswerCount
col_012.description: Number of answers to the question; null for answers.

col_013.name: CommentCount
col_013.description: Number of comments on the post.

col_014.name: FavoriteCount
col_014.description: Number of users who favorited/starred the question; mostly null (only set when nonzero).

col_015.name: LastEditorUserId
col_015.description: Id of the user who last edited the post; references users.col_001. Null when never edited.

col_016.name: LastEditDate
col_016.description: Timestamp of the last edit; null when the post was never edited.

col_017.name: CommunityOwnedDate
col_017.description: Date the post became community wiki (no owner); null for ~97% of posts, matching the rare community-wiki posts. Alternative reading: could mark some other ownership-change event, but community wiki is the standard Stack Exchange meaning.

col_018.name: ParentId
col_018.description: For answers, the id of the parent question (null for questions, ~48% null). Values are post ids; top value 726 has 136 answers.

col_019.name: ClosedDate
col_019.description: Date the post was closed; null for the ~98% of posts that are open. Alternative reading: could be the date of deletion or another lifecycle event, but closure is the standard Stack Exchange meaning.

table.name: tags
table.purpose: Stack Exchange-style tag registry (appears to be from a statistics Q&A site like Cross Validated): one row per tag, with its usage count and links to the posts containing its excerpt and wiki body.

col_003.name: count
col_003.description: Number of times the tag is used (usage count); heavily skewed with a max of 7244.

col_004.name: excerpt_post_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to posts.id for the tag's excerpt (short description) post; null when no excerpt exists. The paired col_005 is consistently one less, matching the Stack Exchange pattern of excerpt and wiki posts created together.

col_005.name: wiki_post_id
col_005.description: Foreign key to posts.id for the tag's full wiki (description) post; null when no wiki exists.

table.name: users
table.purpose: Registered user accounts of a Stack Overflow-style Q&A site (one row per user). Referenced by posts, comments, postHistory, badges and votes as the author/owner of that content.

col_001.name: user_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the user row. Value -1 is the conventional 'community/anonymous' pseudo-user. Referenced by posts, comments, postHistory and badges as the content author.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Id of the user's global account on the parent Q&A network (shared across sites). Most rows share value 101 (a default/placeholder account), so it is not unique per user. Alternative reading: a per-site account identifier that is simply mostly defaulted in this dump.

col_003.name: creation_date
col_003.description: Timestamp when the user account was created (earliest date in table, 2010-07-19, matches site launch).

col_004.name: display_name
col_004.description: Public display name of the user; many auto-generated names like 'user34964' for anonymous registrations.

col_005.name: last_access_date
col_005.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent site visit; always >= creation_date and includes dates up to the data snapshot date.

col_006.name: website_url
col_006.description: Personal website URL from the user's profile; ~80% null, with placeholder values like 'http://none'/'http://N/A' for unset fields.

col_007.name: location
col_007.description: Free-text location from the profile (city/country strings like 'London, United Kingdom', 'Washington DC, United States').

col_008.name: about_me
col_008.description: HTML 'About me' biography text from the profile; ~77% null. Values like 'merge keep'/'please delete me' reflect account-merge/cleanup notes.

col_009.name: up_votes
col_009.description: Count of upvotes cast by the user; heavily zero-skewed, max ~20.9k. Alternative reading: count of upvotes received, though the zero-skew and the paired down_votes column make 'cast' the more likely reading.

col_010.name: down_votes
col_010.description: Count of downvotes cast by the user; more zero-skewed than col_009, max ~11.4k, consistent with downvotes being rarer than upvotes. Alternative reading: count of downvotes received.

col_012.name: views
col_012.description: Number of profile views; unique per row, ranges up to ~5M, -1 for the community pseudo-user. Alternative reading: some other per-user counter, but profile views is the standard Stack Exchange meaning.

col_013.name: age
col_013.description: Self-reported age in years (13-94, median 30); ~79% null since age is optional.

col_014.name: profile_image_url
col_014.description: URL of the user's avatar (gravatar, googleusercontent, facebook graph URLs); the most frequent value is the default identicon avatar.

table.name: votes
table.purpose: One row per vote cast on a post (StackExchange-style schema): up/down votes, favorites, closures, reopenings, bounties, etc., recorded per post and date, with the voter's user id and bounty amount present only for bounty-related vote types.

col_001.name: vote_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the vote record.

col_002.name: post_id
col_002.description: Id of the post (question or answer) the vote was cast on; references posts.col_001 (many votes per post).

col_003.name: vote_type_id
col_003.description: Vote type code. Values 1-16 match StackExchange vote types: 2 = upvote (dominant, 33323), 5 = favorite, 1 = accepted answer, 3 = downvote, 16 = edit, plus others (e.g. 4 = offensive, 6 = close, 7 = reopen, 8 = bounty start, 9 = bounty awarded, 12 = spam, 15 = moderator review). Exact mapping beyond the observed frequencies is inferred from the standard scheme, so another mapping of the rarer codes could also fit.

col_004.name: creation_date
col_004.description: Date the vote was cast (date only, no time), ranging 2010-07-19 to 2011-05-01.

col_005.name: user_id
col_005.description: Id of the user who cast the vote; populated only for vote types that record the voter (e.g. favorites, bounties), hence 91% null. Likely references users, but no accepted join was detected, so it could also be a denormalized voter identifier without an enforced reference.

col_006.name: bounty_amount
col_006.description: Bounty reputation amount (25/50/100/150/200, standard bounty tiers) attached to bounty-related votes; null for all other vote types.
